why: The server-room floor of Megabuilding H11 in Northside: a main room with a netrunner chair, a stairwell down to a technical corridor and the inner server room, which a five-person Tyger Claws crew uses as a subnet hideout. The room shell, doors and devices are always streamed, and the kept global community phase already instantiates the street-story section that owns the crew's workspots, but the community's entries start inactive and vanilla only spawns them from the gig's combat phase. This proposal therefore loads no section and only activates the five Tyger Claws on their ambient states (tagging graffiti, asleep in a chair, patrolling, leaning, at the netrunner chair) instead of the gig's combat staging.

open_questions: Confirm the floor and its workspots exist without our own prefab: the street-story section should already load from the kept Little China community phase, so check the main room, stairwell and server room are physically there before the crew is judged.
Ride the H11 lift to the server-room floor and confirm it is powered, callable and stops at the floor without the gig's scripted ForcePower; report whether the floor terminals are enough.

Walk in as a stranger and confirm the five Tyger Claws stay calm: the floor has a Tyger Claws guard/restricted area (#sts_wat_lch_01_rma_001), so check it does not flag trespass or start combat on sight.
Check the crew is on post and relaxed: one spraying graffiti, one asleep in a chair or netrunner chair, one patrolling, one leaning, one at the netrunner chair; nobody alert or sheltering.
Walk the way in and report which route works: the stairwell glass door, the Body double door into the inner server room, and the Technical Ability vent above the rafters.
Confirm the floor looks intact and unransacked: no halon gas or scene leftovers, no quest graffiti decal frozen mid-spray, no camera lockdown, no upload prompt or disconnected computer.

communities.why: The crew member vanilla moves to #lch_01_ws_painting_graffiti_001 and gives the standing spray-paint workspot: a calm 'tagging the hideout' pose, the right normal-business look for a gang subnet post.

Tatsuya Takei, one of the gig's two named Tyger Claws, on vanilla's own dozing state: the sleep phase drives #lch_01_ws_siting_sleeping_001 and the netrunner-chair spot, which is exactly the slack hideout look rather than a combat stance.
The lookout: vanilla gives him a plain walk patrol (#lch_01_spl_patrol_enemy4_002) and the watching-the-graffiti spots, an unalerted patrol rather than the alert/combat path.
Vanilla's own non-intro phase for this entry, used after the halon intro: a walking patrol and the standing-lean spot, i.e. a calm body in the main room.

Yuri Shaku, the gig's second named Tyger Claw, has only one phase in the registry and it is the community's initial state, so this is the only way to keep him at the post; no spot map resolved, hence the tour check.

deferred_prefab_owner: world streaming (the chosen people need no quest prefab)

proximity_wait.why: The H11 lift controller is a real device entity on the normal way in to the floor (vanilla ForcePowers it in the openworld phase), it streams with the venue in interior_-3_3_0_4, and a proximity wait on it fires when the player arrives at the lift rather than deep inside the server room.
